name: Throttle Down Kustoms Inc.
old_description: We design, engineer, and construct rugged steel front bumpers and rear bumpers for Chevy Silverado, Dodge RAM, Ford F-Series, and GMC Sierra trucks. We also make steel Jeep frames and skid plates. Everything we make is made from CNC laser cut PNO solid steel pate, and hand welded by certified professionals in Moore, Montana, USA. Each truck bumper we offer is better than the factory bumper, and comes with a lifetime warranty.
about:
Throttle Down Kustoms operates from Moore, Montana, where it was established in April 2004 after owner Jeremy Pulse purchased his former employer, Advance Frame Works, and renamed the business. Pulse, a graduate of WyoTech’s Auto Body Technology and Chassis Fabrication program, began building custom truck bumpers in his spare time in the early 2000s before transitioning to full‑time fabrication when demand outgrew his side project.

The company designs, engineers, and builds rugged steel front and rear bumpers for Chevrolet Silverado, Dodge RAM, Ford F‑Series, and GMC Sierra trucks, as well as steel Jeep frames, skid plates, and lightweight aluminum dog boxes for trucks, ATVs, and UTVs. Production relies on CNC laser cutting of 3/16‑inch and 1/4‑inch PNO solid steel plate, CNC mandrel bending of 2"x4" rectangular A500 tubing, and hand welding performed by certified fabricators who have completed recognized chassis‑fabrication programs. All work is carried out in‑house at the Moore facility.

Products serve individual truck owners — ranch hands, off‑road enthusiasts, and commercial users — along with custom‑fabrication clients needing enclosed trailers, rock‑crawling buggies, street rods, and diesel‑powered truggies. The company ships worldwide, with a typical lead time of 8 to 12 weeks for fabricated items.

Throttle Down Kustoms emphasizes domestic manufacturing, a lifetime warranty on every product, and mandrel‑bent frames that are described as sturdier and more precise than welded alternatives. The founder’s commitment to hiring only certified, formally trained fabricators and using U.S.‑sourced steel is presented as the core differentiator.

name: Thunderbird Molding Elkhart
old_description: Realize cost improvements. Reach your performance potential. Get to market quicker. An experienced resource for high-precision custom plastic injection molding and contract manufacturing, we offer comprehensive mold design, prototyping, engineering, production, and assembly services.
about:
Thunderbird Molding operates from Elkhart, Indiana, with additional facilities in Shelbyville, Illinois, and Greensboro. The company is Thunderbird-owned and actively managed, though a founding year and founder names are not publicly disclosed. It began as a resource for high-precision custom plastic injection molding and contract manufacturing.

The shop runs injection molding presses up to 1,500 tons and maintains an inventory of more than 800 molds, supported by a quick-mold-change system and proprietary batch molding procedures. Services span mold design, prototyping, engineering, production, and assembly, including insert molding, over molding (press-to-press transfer), finishing, and secondary operations. A 3D printing cell using carbon printing technology provides an alternative for low-volume end-use parts with properties comparable to injection molding. The company states it holds repeatable tolerances to ±0.0002 in.

Customers come from medical device, automotive, defense, drinkware, and lighting sectors. The firm highlights lens-grade molding for critical defense components and contaminant-free polymers for optical applications. It serves OEMs needing prototype-to-production support, short-run and low-volume orders, and scalable production into the millions.

Thunderbird Molding emphasizes a “performance under pressure” philosophy, citing a 2.5-second cycle time on an 8-cavity mold and a 99% success rate reworking close-tolerance molds to compensate for shrinkage and warpage. Certifications include ISO 9001:2015, ITAR registration, PPAP and SPI compliance, and UL QMMY2 certification.

Projects span marine repairs such as pontoon and skeg work, automotive builds like exhausts, manifolds, roll cages and turbo kits, custom railings (ADA‑compliant), furniture, outdoor fixtures, solar panel frames and mounts, beavertail boat pods, trailer repairs and winch mounts. Customers come from marine, automotive, residential and aerospace sectors. Gabriel emphasizes transparent, upfront pricing with no hidden costs and pledges constant communication until a job is complete. Free quotes are offered on every inquiry. These service commitments are framed as the core differentiators rather than any proprietary technology or certification.

about:
Tin Man Duct Fabrication, based in Manassas, Virginia, has been producing SMACNA-compliant ductwork since 2001. The company serves the greater Washington, D.C. metro area, including Virginia, Maryland, the District, Delaware, and eastern West Virginia.

The shop operates multiple automated production lines to fabricate a full range of ductwork—spiral pipe and fittings, flat oval, TDC, welded stainless, curb adapters, roof rails, and fiberglass-lined products—in materials such as galvanized steel, stainless steel, aluminum, and black iron. Every fitting is inspected and signed by a quality technician before it leaves the facility. The company handles orders from a single fitting up to 400,000-pound projects and delivers to job sites across the region.

Tin Man supplies commercial, industrial, residential, and government contractors. Its customer base includes mechanical contractors who use the shop as a backup when their own fabrication capacity is maxed out, as well as projects requiring LEED-compliant ductwork.

The company differentiates itself by focusing exclusively on ductwork fabrication, avoiding competition with installation contractors. A computerized pricing system provides consistent quotes, and the shop emphasizes fast turnaround, including same-day service on emergency orders.

about:
Tom Simmons Custom Woodworking operates as a sole proprietorship in Des Moines, Iowa, serving homeowners throughout the greater Des Moines metropolitan area. The business is owned and run by Tom Simmons, who works directly with clients on custom cabinetry projects.

The shop fabricates custom kitchen cabinets, bathroom vanities, and built-in furniture pieces. Each project is tailored to the client's specifications, with an emphasis on fit, finish, and integration into existing home architecture. Work is performed in Simmons' workshop using woodworking methods suited to custom one-off production.

Customers are primarily residential homeowners undertaking kitchen and bathroom remodels or new construction, along with occasional contractors seeking custom millwork. The company does not maintain a retail showroom; instead, Simmons shares a portfolio of completed projects on his website and points prospective clients to Google reviews for reference.

Simmons cites quality craftsmanship and attention to detail as the foundation of his reputation, and he aims to deliver cost-effective solutions that enhance the beauty, enjoyment, and long-term value of clients' homes.

name: Tomahawk Manufacturing Inc
old_description: Since 1992, Tomahawk Manufacturing, Inc.®  has been providing the food processing industry with top quality products and services. We thank you for your patronage and look forward to serving you for many more years to come.
about:
Tomahawk Manufacturing Inc was founded in 1992 in Plymouth, Wisconsin. The company began with a mission to provide the food processing industry with an alternative source for spare parts, tooling, and equipment at competitive prices while maintaining high standards of ethics and integrity.

The company designs and manufactures a line of food forming machines — the TM-26, TM-19, TM-400, and TM-6 — capable of throughputs from 1,200 to 6,000 pounds per hour. It also produces custom tooling in-house, supplies spare parts, and provides engineering, field service, training, and automation integration through its Industrial Control Associates division in Albany, Georgia. Operations span a corporate headquarters and manufacturing site in Plymouth, an engineering office in Hartland, Wisconsin, and a European subsidiary in Rijswijk, Netherlands.

Tomahawk serves beef, poultry, seafood, pork, plant-based protein, pet food, and pet pharmaceutical processors worldwide. Its equipment forms products such as beef patties, chicken nuggets, fish cakes, sausages, plant-based proteins, pet treats, and pharmaceutical pills. Customers range from large-scale protein processors to specialty pet treat manufacturers across North America, South America, Europe, and Asia.

The company emphasizes responsive, customer-first support, including 24/7 emergency assistance, on-site service, and comprehensive training programs. Its founding vision — to deliver uncompromising quality and service at competitive rates while maintaining a personal connection with each customer — continues to guide its global operations.

name: Tomfoolery Wood Co.
old_description: Our Pacific Northwest (PNW) furniture balances mid-century modern restraint with natural warmth, using honest materials, natural wood pallets, and thoughtful details to create heirlooms that feel grounded, calm, and deeply connected to our landscape.
about:
Tomfoolery Wood Co. operates from Kent, Washington, in the Pacific Northwest. The company handcrafts custom solid wood furniture in a Seattle-area workshop, building each piece from start to finish.

The shop produces armoires, benches, bookcases, consoles, dressers, vinyl LP storage units, and tables using more than six native Pacific Northwest hardwoods — including Willamette walnut, white oak, maple, cherry, madrone, and myrtle. Wood is hand-selected from responsibly forested sources, with some salvaged from orchards and urban trees at end of life. The team employs waste-minimizing processes and offers custom stain finishes along with solid brass or wood hardware.

The company serves residential clients and design professionals seeking heirloom-quality furniture. Customers have included homeowners in Seattle, Portland, and beyond, with pieces shipped nationally.

Tomfoolery Wood Co. emphasizes sustainability and intentional design, partnering with regional mills and restoration projects to give salvaged wood a second life. The collaborative design process aims to create furniture that tells a story and lasts generations.

name: Tonka Electronics
old_description: ​Tonka Electronics, Inc., was founded on September 1, 1976 as a Manufacturer's Representative and stocking Distributor for the printed circuit board fabrication and assembly industry.  We are a woman owned, small business incorporated in the state of Minnesota.
about:
Tonka Electronics, Inc. was founded on September 1, 1976 in Bloomington, Minnesota as a manufacturer's representative and stocking distributor for the printed circuit board fabrication and assembly industry. The woman-owned small business was incorporated in Minnesota by founder Mike DeLadi, who emphasized a "no slogans, just service" philosophy. Initially focused on representing capital equipment lines, the company expanded into stocking consumables required by that equipment.

Today Tonka operates as a focused distributor specializing in soldering and cleaning products, maintaining a fully stocked warehouse of leaded and lead-free solder bar, wire, and paste, along with fluxes, flux additives, solder masks, and cleaning agents. The company also offers its own SpliceRite line of SMT tape splicing products, cover tape extenders, and carrier tape cutting tools, plus SmartDry intelligent dry storage systems for SMT component reels and trays. Services include manufacturability assessment, process design, technical training, solder analysis, and low-cost resharpening. Tonka supplies spare parts and accessories for Electrovert equipment such as spray fluxers, convection preheaters, chip waves, and nitrogen nozzles, and provides test solutions for Ionograph and OmegaMeter ionic contamination testers.

The company serves the printed circuit board fabrication and assembly sector across its manufacturer's representative territory of Minnesota, North and South Dakota, northwest Wisconsin, and occasionally Iowa. As a distributor, it ships nationwide to electronics manufacturers, including medical device producers who use fine hard wire cutting tools. Customers range from contract manufacturers to OEMs implementing new production lines.

Tonka differentiates itself through deep technical expertise in soldering and cleaning processes, offering both equipment integration support and a broad inventory of consumables available for immediate shipment. The founder's service-first approach remains central, with the company providing free samples of SpliceRite products and hands-on assistance with process development.

about:
Topsy Products operates from Oshkosh, Wisconsin, where it functions as a custom design and fabrication shop focused on the off-road aftermarket. The company does not disclose a founding year, ownership structure, or founder names in its public materials.

The firm designs, engineers, and fabricates hardtop hoist systems, mounting brackets, and related accessories for Jeep Wrangler models (JL, JK, TJ/YJ), the Jeep Gladiator, and the Ford Bronco. It also produces radio communications accessories and a range of branded swag. All items are developed in-house, with the company emphasizing design engineering and development as core steps for every accessory it brings to market. No facility dimensions, headcount, annual volumes, or SKU counts are published.

Customers are primarily individual enthusiasts and retail buyers in the automotive aftermarket, specifically owners of Jeep Wranglers, Gladiators, and Ford Broncos who need hardtop removal and storage solutions. The product lineup also serves users of radio communications gear through dedicated accessory brackets and mounts. Examples from the catalog include JL Hinge Hoist Brackets & Kits, JK Hinge Hoist Brackets & Kits, TJ/YJ Hoist Brackets & Kits, Gladiator Accessories, Door Storage, Ford Bronco Parts, and Radio Communications Accessories.

Topsy Products positions innovation as its guiding principle, stating that creative thinking and attention to detail are key to delivering each item to specification, on budget, and on time. The company frames its differentiation around an innovation-first mindset applied by its staff to every project.

name: Toray Plastics (America), Inc.
old_description: At Toray, we carefully design thoughtful materials that surround you; materials that help keep food fresh, provide protection against the sun’s rays, make cars more luxurious to the touch, add value to industrial applications, and much more.
about:
Toray Plastics (America), Inc. is headquartered in North Kingstown, Rhode Island, with a second operation in Front Royal, Virginia housing its PEF Foam Division. The company is a wholly owned subsidiary of Toray Industries, a Tokyo-based conglomerate established in 1926. No founders are named for the U.S. entity, which operates the Torayfan® and Lumirror® film divisions from its Rhode Island campus.

The manufacturer produces polypropylene and cast polypropylene films under the Torayfan® brand, polyester films under Lumirror®, and metallized OPP, PET, and bio-based PET films. Its PEF Division extrudes polyolefin, polypropylene, and polyethylene foams. Processes include extrusion coating, casting, metallizing, and hot stamping/cold foil. The company describes its equipment as state-of-the-art and says both divisions are global leaders in their respective markets, though facility size, headcount, and volumes are not disclosed.

Toray’s films and foams are sold to converters and manufacturers that fabricate finished goods for packaging, labels, solar-control window films, technical applications, housing and engineering, and automotive markets. The company does not name specific customers but notes its materials are used in food packaging, automotive interiors, and industrial applications.

Toray states its corporate philosophy is to contribute to society through the creation of new value with innovative ideas, technologies, and products, and it emphasizes environmental, social, and governance commitments. The group highlights a sustainability vision addressing climate change, water scarcity, and resource depletion, and holds certifications including ISO 9001, ISO 14001, BRC, Sedex, ISCC PLUS, and Rhode Island Green Manufacturing Certification.
